status.en: 29 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Damascus, Quneitra and Golan Heights.
status.nb: 29 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Damaskus, Quneitra og Golanhøydene.

summary.en: Syria is actively pursuing security cooperation, with its foreign minister confirming talks on joining the Mecca defence pact and officials arresting suspected ISIS members linked to assassinations in Deir Ezzor. Jordan is engaging militarily, stopping an armed group attempting entry from Syria, striking terrorists in retaliation for a church attack, and intercepting millions of drug pills at the Syrian border. Damascus is also expanding diplomatic outreach, participating in Cairo Water Week to discuss agricultural and water cooperation, while seizing large quantities of Captagon and dismantling drug networks. The UCDP recorded 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Syria forfølger aktivt sikkerhetssamarbeid, med utenriksministeren som bekrefter samtaler om å bli med i Mekka-forsvarspakten og tjenestemenn som arresterer mistenkte IS-medlemmer knyttet til attentater i Deir Ezzor. Jordan deltar militært, stopper en væpnet gruppe som forsøkte å komme inn fra Syria, slår ned på terrorister som gjengjeldelse for et kirkebombardement, og avskjærer millioner av narkotika-piller ved grensen mot Syria. Damaskus utvider også diplomatisk kontakt, deltar i Kairo vannuke for å diskutere landbruks‑ og vannsamarbeid, samtidig som de beslaglegger store mengder Captagon og avvikler narkotikamiljøer. UCDP registrerte 2 732 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
background.extract: Disputes and clashes in Syria have continued following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, which many sources consider the end of the Syrian civil war. Numerous actors are involved, including clashes between the newly-formed Syrian caretaker government and later the Syrian transitional government led by the former emir of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) and incumbent president Ahmed al-Sharaa, Assad loyalists, Alawite groups, and Druze insurgents; clashes between elements of the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army (SNA) and the government on one side, and formerly the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on the other; as well as an Israeli invasion and occupation of the demilitarized buffer zone in southwestern Syria.
